draft.title: Plot structure
card: the start of the story. It introduces the characters, the setting and the situation before anything goes wrong.
the problem that disturbs the situation and sets the story moving. After it, the character wants or needs something.
a run of events in which the problem grows harder and the tension builds.
The climax is the turning point, where the tension is highest. The resolution is how things settle afterwards.
draft.remember: A plot moves from a calm start, to a problem, to growing tension, to a peak, to an ending.

a.q: Which part of a plot is the point where the tension is at its highest?
a.why: The climax is the turning point, where tension peaks. The resolution is tempting, but it comes after the climax and shows how things settle.
a.clue: After this point, the story starts to wind down.

b.q: In a story, Priya's dog runs off during a family picnic in the park. Which part of the plot is this moment?
b.why: The dog running off is the problem that disturbs the calm picnic and sets the story moving, so it is the complication. It is not the orientation, which introduces the characters and setting before anything goes wrong.
b.clue: Ask whether this is the start of the problem or the peak of it.
